chunks: My father narrated to us, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: Abdullah bin Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, that he said: Muhammad bin Isa bin Ubaid al-Yaqteeni narrated to me, that he said: Yunus bin Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, from Abdullah bin Sinan, from al-Sadiq, Ja'far bin Muhammad (peace be upon them both), that he said:

Indeed, for Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, are three sanctities which there is nothing like: His Book, which is His Wisdom and Light; His House that He made a destination for the people, by which He accepts no orientation from anyone except (that it is performed) towards it; and the Family of your Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family.

key_terms.صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: Blessings of Allah upon him and his family

ai.seo_question: What are the three sanctities of Allah mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), elevating the 'Itrah to the status of divine sanctities alongside the Quran and the Kaaba, thereby establishing their intrinsic spiritual authority. This triad underscores the Shia theological view that the Prophet's progeny are the living embodiment of divine guidance, inseparable from the revelation they protect and the focal point of worship they embody.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by my father, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Abdullah bin Ja’far al-Himyari, that he said: I was told by Muhammed bin Isa bin Ubaid al-Yaqteeni, that he said: I was told by Yunus bin Abdul-Rahman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from al-Sadiq, Ja’far bin Muhammed, peace be upon them both, that he said:

Indeed, for Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, are three sanctities which there is nothing like: His Book, which is His Wisdom and Light; His House that He made a destination for the people, by which He accepts no orientation from anyone except (that it is performed) towards it; and the Family of your Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family.
